title: The Map Case Chase
markdown:
The plateau wind whipped Zadie awake like a playful giant’s hand. This tug was sharp. Action. Bright sun pricked the caravan shutters. Birds made their case for morning. The tug felt important. Her fingers found the worn leather map case beside the bunk. A secret message inside. Her job: guard it. Ilya’s: deliver it.

“Ready, Zadie?” His voice bounced up the steps, cheerful, already at the lead cart, adjusting a strap. Hawk-sharp eyes on the horizon. “Wind’s picking up. Good for a dash across the flats.”

She thudded down in sturdy boots. “This plateau’s bigger than my hometown. But yes. Dash.” She patted the case. “Needs to get somewhere fast. Thankfully nobody else knows what’s really inside.”

They clattered out. The caravan creaked like a sleepy beast stretching. Wind made her hair dance. Sky went orange, pink, gold. Amazing — and then a flicker. Distant small shapes. The Scythe Gang. They loved maps. They were good at stealing. They had fast ponies.

“Company,” Zadie said, grin tightening.

Ilya’s hand went to the pouch of sketching tools. “Fast. They don’t have my sense of direction.”

“And they don’t have my knack for dodging.” She took the lead reins. “Let’s bounce.”

The caravan lurched, a rumbling beast of burden. Wind howled a wild thrilling song. Behind, a dark dust cloud began to churn and grow. The Scythe Gang galloped, ponies kicking dirt and grit. Shouts, sharp and cruel, cut the wind. Zadie steered with practiced skill, knuckles white, focus laser-sharp on ruts the plateau hid until you were in them. Ilya grabbed a large bundle of spare canvas from the back of the cart, the sort they used when weather forgot its manners.

“They want the case!” he shouted. “They think it’s a treasure map.”

“Let them. We need a distraction. Big.”

She saw it: a narrow rocky gorge in the plateau’s side. “The canvas. Tie it to that jagged rock. Make it flap like a giant startled bird.”

Ilya scrambled, knots fast as a squirrel. The canvas billowed, bright against drab rock, whipped and snapped like something trying to take flight.

Ponies shied. Hooves skittered. A couple of riders slowed — surprise, greed, a giant bird, a trap? That pause was the whole trick.

Zadie yanked right. The caravan plunged down a gentler slope away from the gorge. The wind, suddenly helpful, pushed.

She laughed, wild, the case still tight against her side. Ilya’s eyes sparked. “They’re still gawking. Wondering what kind of magic.”

The dust cloud of the Scythe Gang faded into the vastness, swallowed by plateau. Ahead stretched an endless open expanse, bathed in bright sunshine. The wind kept tugging, but now it felt like a cheer, a whisper onward, onward.

Zadie did not give a speech about courage. She felt the leather under her palm, the secret still unread, Ilya already sketching the gorge from memory so they would not need it twice. He added the canvas-bird in a margin, a joke for later. The morning stayed loud. The case stayed shut. Colors still exploded across the sky as if nothing had tried to steal them. The adventure, as the wind insisted, was just getting its boots on.

“Today,” she said, because the tone of the day would not accept a whisper, “is going to be amazing.”
